title: Your subscription game, connected
subtitle: A visual setup guide for the existing Unity project and its rebuilt PHP backend

pages.title: Follow this setup route
pages.intro: For the game owner or template purchaser setting up the system. You do not need to redesign the Unity scenes.
steps: Prepare
Have an HTTPS host, a database, SMTP credentials, a Stripe test account and Unity ready.
Install the server
Expose only the public folder. Configure the database, game catalog and private environment file.
Connect services
Test email, configure Stripe and schedule the worker commands.
Connect Unity
Set the existing SubscriptionSettings asset, then test registration and a test-mode subscription.
pages.checkpoint: Use the contents on the next page to return to the step you need. Keep the backend URL and Game Identifier consistent throughout.

pages.title: Find your next step
pages.intro: Clickable contents. Each chapter ends with a checkpoint or an expected result.

pages.title: Gather these before starting
pages.intro: The PHP files rebuild the service. They cannot recover the expired server's lost database or old user passwords.
table: Use the version in ProjectVersion.txt: 2022.3.62f3 for this project.
HTTPS, a supported PHP release compatible with PHP 8.2+ code, PDO MySQL, cURL, OpenSSL, mbstring and Argon2id.
A supported MySQL/MariaDB server, a database name, and a database user/password.
Composer and a command line or deployment workflow that can run migrations and scheduled PHP commands.
An SMTP account that permits your chosen sender address.
A test-mode account, recurring prices, Customer Portal configuration and webhook signing secret.
pages.callout: Tested locally with PHP 8.2.12 and MariaDB 10.4.32 in an isolated fixture. Those installed versions are a test record, not a production hosting recommendation. Choose currently supported hosting versions.
pages.checkpoint: Your host must let you expose only public and schedule the worker commands. If it cannot, use a hosting arrangement that can before uploading secrets.

pages.title: What connects to what
pages.intro: Unity is the player-facing app. Your server owns account identity, email delivery and payment verification.
steps: Unity to PHP
Registration and login use the existing PHP filenames. Private calls then carry a session credential.
PHP to services
The server reads its private database and uses SMTP and Stripe with server-only credentials.
Stripe to PHP
Signed events are received, queued and reconciled. Returning from checkout alone does not unlock a plan.
pages.checkpoint: Keep database, SMTP and Stripe secrets on the server. Unity receives a temporary account session, not your server credentials.

pages.title: Upload the right folder
pages.intro: Use Backend/SubscriptionServer as the server project. Only its public directory is reachable by a browser.
steps: Choose the public address
Example: https://example.com/subscriptions. That is the URL you will also enter in Unity.
Place private files outside the document root
Keep src, config, vendor, bin, database, storage and .env private. Do not upload the whole project into a publicly downloadable directory.
Map the URL to public

For a subfolder install, configure an alias or the host's document-root mapping from /subscriptions to the server's public directory. If your host cannot do that safely, use a dedicated subdomain/document root.
pages.checkpoint: A browser should reach public/health.php through your chosen URL. It must not download .env, config/games.php, database files or vendor source.

pages.title: Create a fresh database
pages.intro: Use your host's database panel or an authorized database administrator. This is a clean installation, not an import of old customers.
steps: Create the database
Example name: subscription_game. Enable utf8mb4 and use an InnoDB-compatible database.
Create a database user
Grant the rights needed for migrations during setup. For normal operation, use a user with the required SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE rights.
Record connection values privately
You need host, port, database, username and password. The database host may differ from the website host.
pages.code_caption: Illustrative administrator command. Use your hosting panel if it manages database creation and permissions.
pages.checkpoint: You can connect using the database account intended for setup. Do not use the automated test database command on production data.

pages.title: Fill in the private .env file
pages.intro: Copy .env.example to .env inside SubscriptionServer. Keep the copy outside public and never commit populated secrets.
steps: Set PUBLIC_URL
Use the final HTTPS origin and folder, without a PHP filename. No /public suffix is needed when the document root is mapped correctly.
Generate the installation identifier
Run php bin/generateInstanceId.php after Composer install, then copy its output into BILLING_NAMESPACE. Keep it stable for this installation and use a different value for another deployment.
Keep test and live separate
Start with development and Stripe test credentials. Use separate databases and configuration for production.
pages.checkpoint: Replace every example value you use. Do not paste a Stripe secret, SMTP password or database password into Unity.

pages.title: Install dependencies and tables
pages.intro: Run these commands from Backend/SubscriptionServer, or the matching directory on your server.
pages.code:
composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader
php bin/generateInstanceId.php
php bin/migrate.php
steps: Install the locked dependencies
Composer installs Stripe's PHP SDK, PHPMailer and environment-file support from composer.lock. PHP also needs ZIP support or an extraction tool for Composer archives.
Save the generated identifier
Copy the non-secret identifier into BILLING_NAMESPACE in .env. Keep .env private.
Apply the migrations
Expected result: Database migrations complete. The migration script creates missing tables and records applied migration versions.
pages.callout: If PHP or Composer is not available through your host's command line, ask the host for its supported deployment workflow. This guide does not claim an untested upload-only workaround.
pages.checkpoint: Migrations finish without errors. A second run is safe and reports completion. Do not change migration SQL against real data without a backup and migration review.

pages.title: Give the server your game and plans
pages.intro: Copy config/games.example.php to config/games.php. The private catalog connects a game key to allowed Stripe prices.
pages.code:
'Your Game' => [
  'name' => 'My Game',
  'portal_configuration' => 'bpc_your_test_config',
  'plans' => [
    'monthly' => [
      'name' => 'Monthly',
      'description' => 'Premium access, billed monthly.',
      'price_id' => 'price_your_recurring_test_price',
      'display_price' => 'Your actual amount / month',
      'active' => true,
    ],
  ],
],
steps: Match the game key
The outer key, here Your Game, must exactly match Unity's Game Identifier, including spaces and case.
Map only your allowed prices
Use real recurring test price IDs from Stripe. Display text, amount, currency and renewal wording must match the actual checkout.
Seed the catalog
Run php bin/seed.php. Expected result: Game catalog seeded; retired price mappings retained.
pages.checkpoint: Do not replace the price ID on an existing plan key. Add a new plan key for a new price; omit or disable old offerings while retaining mappings for existing subscribers.

pages.title: Make verification email work
pages.intro: Use development mail logging first, then a real SMTP account. Registration queues verification mail; the mail worker delivers it.
table: log for local development; smtp for real delivery
An authorized sender address and game name
Your email provider's SMTP server and port
Usually tls for port 587; follow your provider
steps: Try the worker
With log transport, read the private storage/mail.log for a development verification link. Never expose that log through the website.
Switch to SMTP
Set MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp and configure your provider. Use a test mailbox and run the worker again.
Verify the account
Open the link within one hour. Expected page: Email verified. Return to Unity and refresh the profile.
pages.checkpoint: The worker reports sent: 1 or more, and the test mailbox receives the link. Production configuration rejects development mail logging. See the troubleshooting chapter for delivery failures.

pages.title: Create recurring test prices
pages.intro: Dashboard navigation can change. The diagram below is illustrative; use the linked official guide for the current Stripe screens.
steps: Stay in the test environment
Create or select the product for your game. Add the recurring prices you want to offer, such as monthly and yearly.
Copy each price ID
Put price_... into the matching entry in config/games.php. Do not use a product ID in the price_id field.
Configure the private API key
Put your test secret key in STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in .env. It must never be placed in the Unity Inspector.
Seed the updated catalog
Run php bin/seed.php and confirm the displayed price/renewal wording matches the hosted checkout.
pages.checkpoint: The catalog contains actual recurring test prices, not price_REPLACE values. Do not run a live purchase during this walkthrough.

pages.title: Connect management and payment updates
pages.intro: The existing Change Plan and Manage buttons open Stripe's Customer Portal through an ownership-checked server link.
steps: Configure the Customer Portal
Enable only the products/prices and operations intended for this game. Decide cancellation timing and plan-change/proration behavior deliberately.
Save the portal configuration
Use its bpc_... identifier in the game's portal_configuration. Separate configurations are required when multiple games share this deployment.
Register the webhook URL
Use your PUBLIC_URL followed by /stripeWebhook.php. Save that endpoint's signing secret as STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
Select the relevant events
Use checkout completion/async outcome, subscription created/updated/deleted, and invoice paid/payment_failed events listed in the server README.
pages.checkpoint: Use the signing secret for this exact endpoint or local CLI listener. Do not mix test/live or CLI/Dashboard webhook secrets.

pages.title: Schedule the maintenance commands
pages.intro: Use your host's scheduler/cron with its absolute PHP executable and the full path to each script. These are CLI commands, not public browser URLs.
table: Every minute; processes up to 100 accounts per run
pages.code_caption: Illustrative Linux cron entries. Replace both paths with your host's real paths.
steps: Check the output
Mail and webhook jobs report counts. Investigate failed counts in private logs; do not publish logs containing verification links.
Recover failed reconciliation
Fix the underlying provider/configuration issue, then use processWebhooks.php --retry-failed for events that exhausted retries.
Run the configuration check
Run php bin/checkConfig.php. Fix every reported issue before testing payments.
pages.checkpoint: Jobs run under the intended server account. Error output is monitored privately. If 100 accounts per pass is too little, adjust worker capacity and monitor reconciliation lag.

pages.title: Connect the existing settings asset
pages.intro: In Unity, choose Tools > Subscription System > Select Settings. This is the same asset already used by Domains in both original scenes.
table: The exact outer key in config/games.php
Keep enabled for the reconstructed backend
Keep the delivered PHP filenames unless you intentionally change the contract
pages.checkpoint: Open LogMasuk and Validate Current Scene. With a configured valid URL, the setup checks should pass. No server password or Stripe secret belongs in this asset.

pages.title: Test registration and verification
pages.intro: Start from the original LogMasuk scene. The client now uses an in-memory credential after login; editable PlayerPrefs flags cannot authenticate an account.
steps: Choose SIGNUP
Enter a test name, valid email, Malaysian mobile number and a password of 12-128 bytes (12-128 characters for ASCII text). A successful result confirms account creation, not email delivery.
Run/check the mail worker
Open the verification link from the test mailbox or private development log. It expires after one hour and is single use.
Choose LOGIN
Sign in with that account. If a previous device session remains active, use the existing authorized logout prompt, then sign in again.
Check the profile
Expected verification state: User Verified after refresh. The server, not the local field, determines this state.
pages.checkpoint: In-memory sign-in intentionally ends after restarting the app. Sign out before closing when practical; otherwise a correct-password device-conflict flow can revoke the old session.

pages.title: Complete a test subscription
pages.intro: Use only your Stripe test environment and the official test payment methods. The existing LANGGAN button is Subscribe.
steps: Open LANGGAN
A verified signed-in user receives a short-lived billing link. Select a plan and confirm its actual amount/currency on Checkout.
Complete the test checkout
Use an official Stripe test payment method. A success page tells you to return to Unity; it does not itself unlock premium content.
Process and refresh
Let the webhook worker run. Return to the game and reopen subscription details if needed. Expected status: ACTIVE with a future access-end date.
Test management
Use the existing plan-change/management controls. Check their effective dates, any amount due and cancellation policy before confirming.
pages.checkpoint: Test renewal failure, cancellation at period end, immediate cancellation and expiry. Active access lasts only through the paid period; other provider states do not silently become ACTIVE.

pages.title: Find the failed checkpoint
pages.intro: Fix the earliest failed checkpoint first. Do not bypass authentication or certificate validation to make a symptom disappear.
table: Set Backend Base Url and the matching game identifier in the existing settings asset.
Check DB host/port/user permissions and that CLI PHP has PDO MySQL enabled.
Run processMail.php, inspect failed counts, verify SMTP sender/credentials and spam folder.
Sign in again. Memory-only credentials do not survive an app restart; revoked sessions cannot be reused.
Use the password-authorized logout action, then retry login. Device name is a label, not proof of identity.
Return to Unity and request a fresh link. Do not bookmark or share ticket URLs.
Check the raw body, signing secret for that endpoint, test/live environment and server clock.
Run webhook/reconciliation jobs. Verify mapped recurring price, period end and provider status; refresh Unity.
Retry the same plan. If an old intent needs repair, reconcile provider records before creating another subscription.
Correct the game's portal configuration and allowed price catalog before continuing.
pages.checkpoint: When reporting an issue, include the step and non-sensitive error code. Remove passwords, credentials, verification links and billing tickets from screenshots/logs.

pages.title: Before you switch to live
pages.intro: Passing local tests is not a deployment or a real payment test. Complete this checklist in your own hosting and device environment.
steps: Separate production
Use a production database, SMTP setup, live Stripe credentials and live webhook endpoint. Keep a unique stable installation namespace.
Enable live mode explicitly
Set APP_ENV=production and ALLOW_LIVE_PAYMENTS=true only when ready. Use SMTP; development mail logging is blocked.
Verify distribution requirements
Choose the billing integration appropriate for your target platform/store before release. This project does not add native store billing.
Back up and monitor
Back up private configuration and database, monitor failed mail/webhooks and reconciliation lag, and test a restore procedure.
pages.checkpoint: Do not recreate old paid subscriptions to recover lost users. Historical account/customer recovery needs a separate ownership-verified migration, not an email-only match.
